task_title: Isolate the e2e lab server port and unblock docs:check

plan_review.notes: Reviewer found no blocking issues. Addressed: narrowed externalLinkLabelRanges so same-page #anchor labels are still validated; added a setup-level regression test that global-setup rejects an occupied port before spawning Vite; verified the occupied-port path live (the run aborts in ~1s with the actionable message); clarified that process.execPath spawning was pre-existing, not part of this diff. RESIDUAL LIMITATION (disclosed, not fixed): the reporter's failures were on Windows and this sandbox is Linux, so the port-collision root cause is strongly inferred rather than directly observed on the maintainer's machine. Not weakened or hidden - it is called out as a known validation gap in the PR description and the handoff so a human can rerun the two commands on Windows.

rounds.notes: Medium: isPortInUse only probed 127.0.0.1, so an IPv6-only squatter read as free. Medium: check-then-spawn race meant a bare port probe could accept a foreign listener that grabbed the port after preflight. Fixed: isPortInUse probes ::1 and 127.0.0.1; readiness now requires our own child Vite ready banner (ANSI-stripped, port-matched) before the port probe, raced against child exit/error. Regression tests added for both.

Medium: dual-stack bind race - IPv4- and IPv6-specific listeners can coexist, so a banner from our child plus a family-agnostic probe/URL could still route the browser to a foreign ::1 server. Fixed by forcing one address family end to end: E2E_LAB_HOST=127.0.0.1 in the base URL, --host 127.0.0.1 on the Vite spawn, and waitForPort probing that exact host only. Re-verified: 28/28 e2e, 21/21 unit, tsc clean. Round 3 reply: both prior findings resolved, no new high-confidence issues.
Re-review after the address-family pinning: 'Both prior code findings are resolved. No new high-confidence issues found in the reviewed changes.'

independent_grade.notes: The diff correctly isolates the e2e lab server port by adding a dedicated e2eLab offset, avoiding conflicts with interactive labs. It effectively verifies the port ownership by awaiting Vite's ready banner, handling dual-stack IPv4/IPv6 edge cases. The changes precisely target the stated issue with excellent unit test coverage, and documentation check blocks are removed cleanly while leaving necessary validation intact. Code quality, comments, and adherence to repository policies are excellent.
